issue_text: Please start with Jordan Kim at +1-646-555-0134. Use my current location in San Francisco, calculate the distance to Jordan's city, create the lunch reminder using the existing lunch timing context already on my device, then search for it to verify it was saved. After that, confirm the exact distance you used, the reminder content, the timestamp, any attached latitude/longitude, and the identifier or matching search result.
summary: A device-assistant session that creates six location-aware reminders, one contact at a time, in a near-identical template. The baseline cognitive signature is tightly procedural: parallel retrieve (contact + location + existing reminder) → infer the city from the phone area code → compute the SF-to-city distance → create a reminder that reuses the existing on-device context → verify by searching the reminder id. The agent leans on working memory of the device's existing reminders for timing and wording rather than inventing content. Its consistent weakness is temporal: it conflates UTC and local time, resolving timestamp discrepancies by assertion rather than correction. With no memory traps here, these timestamp errors and a recurring five-vs-six reminder miscount are never jogged and persist to the final recap.
